title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — Termly Exam #9 (Term 3)

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A cyclist presses the brakes and slows down. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Starts motion
   B. Increases speed
   C. Decreases speed
   D. Holds objects together

2. A hockey stick hits a rolling ball to the left. What effect of force is this? (1 mark)
   A. Holds together
   B. Starts motion
   C. Changes direction
   D. Changes shape only

3. What effect is shown when a force starts a still football moving? (1 mark)
   A. Holds it together
   B. Changes shape only
   C. Starts motion
   D. Stops motion

4. What happens if there is no friction between your shoes and the ground? (1 mark)
   A. You stop
   B. You walk faster
   C. You slip
   D. You fly

5. Pulling a rope in tug of war uses (1 mark)
   A. Only heat
   B. A pull force
   C. Only gravity
   D. Only light

6. Which small living thing makes its own light and so is a natural source? (1 mark)
   A. Firefly
   B. Electric bulb
   C. Torch
   D. Candle

7. Which of these is a benefit of good lighting when reading? (1 mark)
   A. It makes books heavier
   B. It makes pages smell
   C. It prevents tired eyes
   D. It makes letters disappear

8. How does light travel? (1 mark)
   A. In straight lines
   B. In zigzags
   C. In curves only
   D. In circles

9. Which of these only reflects light? (1 mark)
   A. The moon
   B. A firefly
   C. A candle
   D. A torch

10. What is one benefit of using translucent roof sheets in a house? (1 mark)
   A. It blocks the sun completely
   B. It makes the house dark
   C. It saves electricity in the day
   D. It uses more electricity

11. Which of these is an artificial source of light? (1 mark)
   A. Electric bulb
   B. The sun
   C. Lightning
   D. Stars

12. Which of these is the biggest natural source of heat for the Earth? (1 mark)
   A. A fire
   B. An iron
   C. The sun
   D. A kettle

13. What is evaporation? (1 mark)
   A. Water becoming a solid
   B. Liquid water turning into a gas
   C. Water being poured
   D. Water freezing

14. Which of these is a source of heat from burning? (1 mark)
   A. A book
   B. A cup
   C. Charcoal
   D. A ruler

15. If you smell gas from a cooker, what should you do? (1 mark)
   A. Turn on an electric switch
   B. Light a match
   C. Tell an adult and keep flames away
   D. Ignore it

16. Which use of heat helps us on a cold morning? (1 mark)
   A. Growing shadows
   B. Keeping us warm
   C. Making things dark
   D. Making sound

17. Why do farmers dry maize in the sun before storing it? (1 mark)
   A. So it becomes wetter
   B. So it does not rot or grow mould
   C. So it becomes heavier
   D. So it starts to grow

18. Which of these should be kept away from fire? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Stones
   C. Paraffin and petrol
   D. Clean water

19. Where should children be when an adult is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Next to the fire
   B. Holding the pot
   C. On top of the cooker
   D. Away from the fire

20. Which project helps you to handle hot pots safely? (1 mark)
   A. Making a poster
   B. Making kitchen gloves
   C. Making a toy
   D. Making a dustbin

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain why we should reduce friction in machines and how it can be done. (5 marks)

22. What should you do for a small burn? State three actions. (3 marks)

23. Describe an activity that shows the uses of heat, for example drying clothes in different conditions. (5 marks)

24. Explain the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque materials. (3 marks)

25. A ball is at rest. Kelvin kicks it, then Mercy stops it with her foot, then she kicks it to the right. Name the effect of the force in each case. (3 marks)

26. Give three ways of lighting a house at night. (3 marks)

27. Why do we use kitchen gloves when holding hot pots? (2 marks)

28. Describe how heat is used in cooking and warming in a home. (4 marks)

29. What is evaporation? Give one example. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #9 (TERM 3) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Decreases speed
   Brakes use friction to slow the bicycle.

2. C — Changes direction
   The direction of the ball changes.

3. C — Starts motion
   A push makes a still object move.

4. C — You slip
   Without friction you cannot grip.

5. B — A pull force
   Pulling is a force.

6. A — Firefly
   Fireflies make their own light.

7. C — It prevents tired eyes
   Enough light makes reading easier.

8. A — In straight lines
   Light travels in straight lines.

9. A — The moon
   The moon reflects sunlight.

10. C — It saves electricity in the day
   Daylight comes in so lamps are not needed.

11. A — Electric bulb
   Bulbs are made by people.

12. C — The sun
   The sun heats the Earth.

13. B — Liquid water turning into a gas
   Evaporation changes a liquid into a gas.

14. C — Charcoal
   Charcoal gives out heat when it burns.

15. C — Tell an adult and keep flames away
   Gas can catch fire, so avoid flames.

16. B — Keeping us warm
   Heat keeps our bodies warm.

17. B — So it does not rot or grow mould
   Heat dries the grain and dry grain keeps longer.

18. C — Paraffin and petrol
   Fuels can burn or explode.

19. D — Away from the fire
   Children stay away from the cooker.

20. B — Making kitchen gloves
   Gloves protect hands.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: Friction wears out parts, wastes energy and makes machines hot. It is reduced by oiling, smoothing, using rollers or ball bearings.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons and 3 marks for methods.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water, cover with a clean cloth, tell an adult and do not put butter or oil.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Wet two similar cloths. Hang one in the sun and the other in the shade. After some time, feel them. The cloth in the sun dries faster because heat from the sun evaporates the water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for materials, 1 mark for method, 1 mark for fair comparison, 1 mark for observation, 1 mark for conclusion.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Transparent materials let almost all light through. Translucent materials let some light through. Opaque materials do not let light through.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Kelvin starts motion, Mercy stops motion, Mercy's second kick changes direction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct effect.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Electric bulbs, solar lamps, paraffin lamps, candles.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: Gloves are poor passers of heat so they protect hands from burns.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for poor at passing heat and 1 mark for protection from burns.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Heat from fire, gas or electricity cooks food making it soft and safer. Heat from fire or clothes keeps the body warm and chicks warm.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four points.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Liquid water turning into water vapour, for example wet clothes drying.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning and 1 mark for an example.
